Rashi on Pesachim 73b:10:1.hebrew: ואי רבי אליעזר - אמאי תנן מתני' פטור? לחייב משום שבת, דהא לית ליה כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:10:1.english: And if [it is] Rabbi Eliezer - Why did our Mishnah teach [that he is] exempt? Let him be liable [to bring a sin-offering] on account of Shabbat, for he does not hold [that one who errs in regard to a mitzvah is exempt], etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:11:1.english: And with regard to exemptions - [the exemptions] of one who errs in a matter of a mitzvah.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:11:2.english: He holds - Rabbi Yosef ben Ḥonai [holds] in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:12:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר רב דאמר - לעיל לא בעי עקירה, לית ליה דהאי תנא דאמר בחול ישרף מיד. אלא קסבר רב, דמתניתין לענין צורה כי האי תנא סבר לה, דאמר בעי עיבור צורה:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:12:1.english: Rav Ashi said: Rav, who said - above [that] it does not require uprooting, does not hold like that Tanna who says [that] on a weekday it is burned immediately. Rather, Rav holds that our Mishnah, with respect to [decay of] form, holds like this Tanna, who says it requires decay of form.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:12:2.hebrew: אם יש שהות ביום - לזה ששחט פסח זה בשבת לבדוק אם מתו בעלים כו' ולא שאל, לא טועה בדבר מצוה הוא, אלא שוגג וחייב. שוגג קרי את הקרוב לפושע:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:12:2.english: If there is time in the day - for this [person] who slaughtered this Paschal offering on Shabbat to check whether the owners died, etc., and he did not ask — he is not [considered] one who erred in [the performance of] a mitzvah, but rather an unwitting transgressor, and he is liable. [The baraita] calls one who is close to being negligent an "unwitting transgressor."

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:12:3.hebrew: ותעובר צורתו - אם הוא חול, דאילו בשבת לא אצטריך ליה, דהא בשבת לא שריף ליה, ולמחר ביום טוב נמי לא שריף ליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:12:3.english: And its form must decay - [This applies] if it is a weekday; for on Shabbat, [this ruling] would not be necessary, since on Shabbat he does not burn it, and tomorrow on Yom Tov he also does not burn it.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:12:4.english: What is the reason - [that] it requires decay of [its] form?

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:12:5.hebrew: לאו משום דקסבר לא בעי עקירה - וזה סתם נשחט, והרי הוא שלמים כשרין, אלא שנשחטו אחר התמיד, ופסול מחמת דבר אחר הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:12:5.english: Is it not because he holds [it] does not require uprooting - And this [offering] was slaughtered without specification, and behold, it is a valid peace-offering, except that it was slaughtered after the daily offering, and it is a disqualification due to another factor.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:13:1.hebrew: וממאי דילמא - לעולם בעי עקירה ופסולו בגופו, והאי דבעי עיבור צורה, משום דרבי ישמעאל סבר לה כתנא דבי רבה בר אבוה, דאמר אפילו פיגול שפסולו בגופו טעון עיבור צורה. ולא איתפריש לי עיקר מילתיה דתנא דרבה בר אבוה היכא אתמר, ובכמה מקומות מייתי לה בגמרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:13:1.english: And from where [is this known]? Perhaps - Actually, it requires uprooting and its disqualification is in its own body [i.e., inherent], and the reason he requires decay of form is because Rabbi Yishmael agrees with the tanna of the school of Rabbah bar Avuh, who said [that] even piggul, whose disqualification is in its own body, requires decay of form. And it was not made clear to me where the primary statement of the tanna of [the school of] Rabbah bar Avuh was stated, though in several places [the Gemara] cites it.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:14:1.hebrew: דאי לא תימא הכי - דטעמא משום דקסבר פסול הגוף טעון עיבור צורה, אלא משום דלא בעי עקירה, הא תינח מתו או נתכפרו; אבל נטמאו, מי איכא דלא בעי עקירה? הא סתמיה לפסח שני קאי, ורבי ישמעאל "או שנטמאו" נמי קתני:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:14:1.english: For if you do not say so - [that is,] that the reason is because he holds [that] a physical disqualification requires leaving [the offering] overnight to lose its form (ibbur tzurah), [and you say] rather [that it is] because it does not require uprooting, this works well [where the owners] died or achieved atonement [with another offering]; but [where] they became ritually impure, is there [anyone who says] that it does not require uprooting? Behold, by default it stands for the second Pesach, and Rabbi Yishmael also teaches "or if they became ritually impure."

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:15:1.hebrew: אלא מחוורתא - דטעמא דרבי ישמעאל משום דקסבר פסול הגוף טעון עיבור צורה, ותנא דישרף מיד סבר לא בעי עיבור צורה. ואי לתרוצי בעית דלא תיקשי לרב, הכי תרצת, דפסול הגוף דידה גבי מתו או משכו ידם משום דשחטיה לשם פסח בהדיא, ואיהו לשלמים קאי בלא עקירה כרב, והוו להו שלמים לשם פסח, ופסול הגוף הוא כיוסף בן חונאי:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:15:1.english: Rather, it is clear - that the reason of Rabbi Yishmael is because he holds [that] an invalidation of the body [of the offering] requires disfigurement [of its form], whereas the Tanna [who teaches] "it shall be burned immediately" holds [that] it does not require disfigurement [of its form]. And if you wish to resolve [it] so that it does not pose a difficulty to Rav, thus you resolve [it]: that its invalidation of the body in the case where [the owners] died or withdrew their hands is because he slaughtered it explicitly for the sake of a Pesach offering, while it stands as a peace-offering without uprooting [its status], in accordance with Rav, and thus it is a peace-offering [slaughtered] for the sake of a Pesach offering, and it is an invalidation of the body, in accordance with Yosef ben Chonai.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:1:1.english: And it was taught regarding it - [that is,] our Mishnah.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:1:2.english: On a weekday, in a case like this - Since he is able to burn it.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:1:3.hebrew: ישרף מיד - ואין צריך להמתין עד שתעבור צורתו. ואע"ג דמותר הפסח קרב שלמים, ואם היה שוחטו לזה שמתו בעליו לשם שלמים היה כשר, עכשיו שלא עקר שם פסח ממנו — ישרף מיד, דהוה ליה פסח שנשחט שלא למנויו:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:1:3.english: It should be burned immediately - And it is not necessary to wait until its form decays. And even though a leftover Paschal offering is offered as a peace-offering, and had he slaughtered this [animal] whose owners died for the sake of a peace-offering it would have been valid — now that he did not uproot the designation of a Paschal offering from it, it should be burned immediately, since it is [like] a Paschal offering that was slaughtered not for its registrants.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:1:4.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא - אע"ג דסתמיה לשם שלמים קאי, בעי עקירה, וכל כמה דלא עקר, הוי שם פסח עליו. משום הכי ישרף מיד, ולא בעי עיבור צורה, דהוה ליה פסולו בגופו, שנשחט שלא למנויו:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:1:4.english: Granted, if you say - Even though its unspecified [status] stands for the sake of a peace offering, it requires uprooting, and as long as [one] has not uprooted [it], the designation of a Paschal offering remains upon it. Therefore, it should be burned immediately, and does not require passing of form [waiting overnight], for its disqualification is in its body [itself], since it was slaughtered not for its registered [owners].

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:2:1.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת לא בעי עקירה - וסתמיה שלמים הוא, פסולו מחמת מאי הוי, הואיל ושלמים הוא? משום דנשחט אחר תמיד בין הערבים — דשחיטת פסח אחר התמיד היא, כדאמר בתמיד נשחט (דף נט:) — ועבר על עשה דהשלמה:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:2:1.english: But if you say [that] it does not require uprooting - and by default it is a peace-offering, due to what is its disqualification, since it is a peace-offering? Because it was slaughtered after the daily afternoon offering — for the slaughtering of the Paschal offering is after the daily offering, as is stated in [the chapter] Tamid Nishchat (59b) — and he transgressed the positive commandment of completion.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:3:1.hebrew: כל שפסולו בגופו - כגון פיגול, נותר, טמא ויוצא — ישרף מיד, ואין צריך להמתין:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:3:1.english: Any whose disqualification is in its body - Such as piggul, notar, [that which is] impure, or [that which] went out [of its permitted boundary] — it should be burned immediately and does not need to wait.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:3:2.hebrew: בדם ובבעלים - כגון נשפך הדם, וכגון פסח שמתו בעלים או נטמאו אחר זריקה, דעכשיו פסח כשר הוא, אלא שאין לו אוכלין:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:3:2.english: In the blood and in the owners - For example, [where] the blood was spilled, or, for example, a Paschal lamb whose owners died or became impure after the sprinkling [of the blood], for now it is a valid Paschal lamb, except that it has no one to eat it.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:3:3.hebrew: תעובר צורתו - ימתינו לו עד שתעובר ממנו צורת בשר, דכיון דאין פסולו חמור, לא שרפינן קדשים בבזיון. ועיבור צורה הוא פסול לינה, דהוה ליה פסולו בגופו:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:3:3.english: Its form shall decay - They wait for it until the form of meat passes from it, for since its disqualification is not severe, we do not burn consecrated [offerings] in a disgraceful manner. And "decay of form" is the disqualification of being left overnight, for it is [then] a disqualification in its own body.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:5:1.hebrew: ולר' חייא בר גמדא - דאמר בתמיד נשחט (דף סד.) גבי מתניתא דקתני התם דפסח בעי עקירה, ואוקמה כגון שהיו בעלים טמאי מתים כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:5:1.english: And according to Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda - Who said in [the chapter] Tamid Nishchat (daf 64a), regarding the baraita that teaches there that a Pesach [offering] requires uprooting, and he established it [as referring to a case] such as where the owners were impure from a corpse, etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:6:1.hebrew: הא - אחר דלאו סתמא קאי לפסח, לא בעי עקירה:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:6:1.english: But - another [offering] that does not stand by default for a Pesach [offering] does not require uprooting.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:6:2.hebrew: מאי איכא למימר - כלומר, מתני' דהכא תיובתיה, דקתני ישרף מיד, ולא מיתוקמא אלא משום עקירה:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:6:2.english: What is there to say - That is to say, the Mishnah here is a refutation of him, for it teaches: it shall be burned immediately, and it can only be established because of [the requirement of] uprooting.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:7:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע - לעולם כדקאמר, שחטו סתם כשר לעולה, דכיון דקאי לעולה סתמיה עולה הוא, ואע"פ שתחלתו אשם. וכן מותר הפסח, כיון דלשלמים קאי, סתמא כי שחיט ליה שלמים הוא. והכא דקתני ישרף מיד, לאו משום עקירה, אלא כגון שהפרישו קודם חצות, וכי מטא חצות קבעתיה חצות שהוא זמן שחיטתו, ונראה לפסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:7:1.english: Rather, Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said - Actually, [it is] as he says: [if] one slaughtered it without specification, it is valid as a burnt-offering, for since it stands [designated] for a burnt-offering, its unspecified [slaughter] is a burnt-offering, even though its initial [designation] was a guilt-offering. And similarly, a leftover Paschal offering: since it stands [designated] for a peace-offering, when one slaughters it without specification, it is a peace-offering. And here, where [the Mishnah] teaches that it is burned immediately, [it is] not because of uprooting [its designation], but rather [in a case] where he designated it before midday, and when midday arrived, midday — which is the time of its slaughter — established it, and it became fit for the Paschal offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:7:2.hebrew: ומתו בעלים אחר חצות - ונדחה מפסח, דשוב אינו חוזר ונראה לשלמים. והא דקי"ל מותר הפסח אחר הפסח קרב שלמים — כגון שאבד קודם חצות ונמצא אחר שחיטת הפסח, דלא אתא חצות עליה למיקבעה, ולא נראה לשחיטת פסח מעולם:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:7:2.english: And the owners died after midday - and it was rejected from [being] a Paschal offering, so that it does not again become fit for peace-offerings. And [as for] that which we hold [that] a leftover Paschal offering after Passover is offered [as] peace-offerings — [that is in a case] such as where it was lost before midday and found after the slaughtering of the Paschal offering, so that midday did not come upon it to establish it, and it was never fit for the slaughtering of the Paschal offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:8:1.hebrew: מידי הוא טעמא אלא לרב - האי תירוצא רב מתריץ ליה, דאמר לא בעי עקירה:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:8:1.english: Is this reason [necessary] for anyone but Rav - Rav is the one who gave this answer, as he said [that it] does not require uprooting.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:8:2.english: And didn't Rav say - In the chapter [entitled] Shenei Se'irei.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:8:3.hebrew: בעלי חיים אינן נדחין - ואין דיחוי אלא בדם או בבעלים, כגון שעיר של שם שנשחט, וקודם זריקת דמו מת המשתלח — ישפך הדם; אבל כל זמן שהקרבן חי, אינו נפסל משום דיחוי:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:8:3.english: Living creatures cannot be rejected - And there is no rejection except with blood or with the owners — for example, the goat [designated] for the Name [of God] that was slaughtered, and before the sprinkling of its blood the [goat] sent away [to Azazel] died, [in which case] the blood must be poured out; but as long as the offering is alive, it is not disqualified on account of rejection.

Rashi on Pesachim 73b:9:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רב פפא - לעולם לא בעי עקירה, וסתמיה שלמים. והא דקתני עלה דמתניתין "בחול ישרף מיד" — ר' אליעזר הוא, ומשום דשלמים הוא, וכגון דשחטיה בהדיא לשם פסח. ורבי אליעזר לטעמיה, דאמר בפרק תמיד נשחט (פסחים דף סב:): שלמים ששחטן לשם פסח, פסול:
Rashi on Pesachim 73b:9:1.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said - In fact, [it] does not require uprooting [of its designation], and by default [it is] a peace-offering. And that which is taught [in the baraita] regarding our Mishnah, "on a weekday it must be burned immediately," is [the opinion of] Rabbi Eliezer — and [its disqualification is inherent] because it is a peace-offering, and [it refers to] a case where he explicitly slaughtered it for the sake of a Paschal offering. And Rabbi Eliezer follows his [own] reasoning, as he said in the chapter [entitled] Tamid Nishchat (Pesachim 62b): Peace-offerings that one slaughtered for the sake of a Paschal offering are disqualified.

Tosafot on Pesachim 73b:2:1.hebrew: פסולו מחמת מאי הוי ששחטו כו' - וא"ת: מאי קמדמי הך עקירה לההיא דלעיל, דאשם שכפרו בעליו באחר — תו לא חזי לאשם, אבל פסח שנטמאו בעליו או משכו ידיהם — אכתי חזי לפסח אם ימנו אחרים עליו, כדתנן לקמן (פסחים דף פט.): "נימנין ומושכין ידיהם עד שישחט"? וי"ל: דהני מילי כשנשאר אחד מבני חבורה עליו, שאם נשאר לגמרי בלא בעלים — תו לא חזי לפסח, כדתניא בסוף מי שהיה טמא (לקמן פסחים צח.): "המפריש פסח ומת — אם בנו נמנה עליו, יביאנו לשם פסח; אין בנו נמנה עליו, יביאנו לשם שלמים":
Tosafot on Pesachim 73b:2:1.english: "Due to what is its disqualification, that he slaughtered it, etc." - And if you ask: How can [the Gemara] compare this uprooting to that [case] above, for a guilt-offering whose owners gained atonement through another [animal] is no longer fit to be a guilt-offering, whereas a Paschal offering whose owners became impure or withdrew their hands [from it] is still fit to be a Paschal offering if others register for it, as we learned in the Mishnah later (Pesachim 89a): "[People] may register and withdraw their hands until it is slaughtered"? And one can answer: That applies [only] when one of the members of the group remains [registered] on it, for if it is left completely without owners, it is no longer fit to be a Paschal offering, as it was taught in a Baraita at the end of [the chapter] Mi Shehayah Tamei (below, Pesachim 98a): "One who sets aside a Paschal offering and dies — if his son registers for it, he brings it as a Paschal offering; [if] his son does not register for it, he brings it as a peace-offering."

Tosafot on Pesachim 73b:3:1.hebrew: בדם ובבעלים תעובר - תימה, א"כ היכי קתני: "שחטו ונודע שמשכו בעלים את ידם או שנטמא בחול — ישרף מיד"? והא בדם ובבעלים בעינן עיבור צורה! וליכא למימר כפי' הקונטרס, דהך דבדם ובעלים מיירי כגון שנטמא אחר זריקה, דעכשיו פסח כשר אלא שאין לו אוכלין; דבפרק כיצד צולין (לקמן פסחים פב:) מוקמינן לה קודם זריקה, דקתני בעלים דומיא דדם. ותירץ ר' שמואל בר' שלמה דההיא דלעיל מיירי קודם שחיטה, דהוי כמו שחטו שלא לאוכליו, דחשיב פסולו בגופו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 73b:3:1.english: In the blood or in the owners, [its form] is allowed to decay - [This is] astonishing! If so, how does [the baraita] teach: "If he slaughtered it and it became known that the owners withdrew their hands [from it], or that [the owner] became impure, on a weekday — it should be burned immediately"? But in [a case of disqualification] in the blood or in the owners, we require decay of form! And one cannot say like the explanation of the Kunteres [Rashi], that this [case] of "in the blood or in the owners" is speaking of a case such as where [the owner] became impure after the sprinkling [of the blood], for now the Paschal offering is valid except that it has no eaters; because in the chapter Keitzad Tzolin (below, Pesachim 82b), we establish it [as referring to] before the sprinkling, since it teaches "owners" similar to "blood." And Rabbi Shmuel son of Rabbi Shlomo resolved [the difficulty] that that [baraita] above is speaking of before slaughter, which is like one who slaughtered it for those who cannot eat it, which is considered [a case where] its disqualification is in its body itself.

Tosafot on Pesachim 73b:8:1.hebrew: האמר רב בעלי חיים אינם נדחין - תימא, הא מסקי' בפ' שני שעירי (יומא סד:): "אמר לך רב: אליבא דר' יהודה לא קאמינא"; וא"כ, לימא דמתניתין רבי יהודה דסבר נדחין! וכמה משניות מצינו דסברי דבעלי חיים נדחין — בפ' מי שהיה טמא (לקמן פסחים צח.), ובתמורה (דף כב.), ובשילהי כריתות (דף כח.) — דדייק עלייהו: "שמע מינה בעלי חיים נדחין", וצריך לרב לאוקמי' כרבי יהודה; ומתני' נמי אמאי לא מוקי כוותיה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 73b:8:1.english: But Rav said: Living creatures are not [permanently] rejected - This is difficult: behold, we conclude in the chapter [entitled] Shenei Se'irei (Yoma 64b): "Rav would say to you: According to Rabbi Yehudah, I did not say [that living creatures are not rejected]"; and if so, let [the Gemara] say that our Mishnah is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehudah, who holds that they are rejected! For we find several mishnayot that hold that living creatures are rejected — in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shehayah Tamei (below, Pesachim 98a), and in Temurah (22a), and at the end of Keritot (28a) — regarding which [the Gemara] infers: "Learn from this that living creatures are rejected," and Rav is forced to establish them as [following] Rabbi Yehudah; so why does he not establish our Mishnah as well in accordance with him?
